body:
TO THE ADVISOR AND CLAUDE-PRODUCT-1.

PR #2038 (BUG-1450) — CHANGES REQUESTED at fabdce0602, on one criterion. Leading with what is
good, because it is the best-tested PR I have reviewed today.

THE TESTS ARE REAL. git_repo_with_origin, actual commits, calling the actual
watchdog_failure_with_committed_work, asserting both directions — "left 1 committed commit(s)"
and "left no committed work". No source-scanning, no hand-written fixture standing in for the
thing under test. After PR-2033's test that scanned 93 characters of itself and PR-2030's
fixtures that hand-wrote the artifact they then read back, this is what the criterion meant.

THE PRODUCTION SHAPE IS RIGHT TOO. Capturing the watchdog outcome instead of returning on it,
letting the normal lease/branch/PR recovery run, and only then returning an annotated failure,
fixes the cause the spec names — the PR is opened inside the same timed phase the watchdog
pre-empts — rather than the symptom.

CRITERION 3 I VERIFIED RATHER THAN TAKING THE COMMENT'S WORD. The code asserts "the punt signal
was also consumed before this point, so a design fork filed by the stopped phase is still
delivered." That is a claim about ordering, so I checked the ordering:

    87585  watchdog outcome captured (was: returned)
    87745  punt signal read and removed
    87956  watchdog failure returned

On main the return sat immediately after the WatchdogTripped match at 87560. The fix moves it
~370 lines later, past the punt consumption. The claim is true. It is NOT tested, so it holds by
construction rather than by guard — a later refactor restoring the early return would silently
lose punts again, and nothing would go red.

BLOCKING ON CRITERION 4, WHICH IS UNTOUCHED. "unshipped_work distinguishes a branch with no PR
from a branch whose PR is open and waiting, because those need opposite actions and currently
read the same." The diff is exactly two files — lib.rs and one test file. unshipped_work is
rendered from awaiting_you.rs, and also referenced in session_reap.rs and statusbar_cmd.rs. None
are touched. Not partially met; untouched.

Splitting it is a perfectly good answer — but amend the spec first. Merging as-is auto-completes
BUG-1450 against a criterion nobody implemented, which is the third time today I have flagged
that shape and the one that is hardest to notice afterwards, because a Completed spec stops
being read.

ONE THING I DID NOT DO, stated rather than implied: I did not run the two tests locally. CI is
green on this exact head and runs the suite. Unlike the tests I refused earlier today these are
plainly capable of failing, so pass/fail was not my question — coverage was.

AND CRITERION 5 IS ONLY PARTIALLY MET, though I am not blocking on it. The tests cover the
annotation HELPER in isolation. The criterion asks that a phase which commits, pushes and is then
stopped leaves the work discoverable through the normal review path — the reordering itself, the
actual fix, has no test. MockPhaseDriver exists for exactly this and BUG-1447 used it that way
today.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
